reference_items.stem:
Central School had a bottle collection. Children in each class brought empty bottles to school. The principal made a bar graph of the number of bottles from five classes.

[Image: Bar graph of number of bottles collected by five classes]

Which class collected 45 bottles?
reference_items.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number of Bottles" marked from 0 to 100 with horizontal grid lines every 20 units (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). The horizontal axis shows five classes:
- "Miss Barber’s Class": bar reaches 80.
- "Mr. Chyn’s Class": bar reaches approximately 45 (just above 40, a quarter of the way to 60).
- "Mrs. Friedman’s Class": bar reaches 80.
- "Miss Gonzalez’s Class": bar reaches approximately 87.
- "Mr. Mack’s Class": bar reaches approximately 70 (halfway between 60 and 80).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

Which graph shows the same information as the pie chart?

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart titled "Favorite Subject" is divided into five sectors: Math (the largest sector, about one-third of the circle), Science (the second largest, about one-fourth of the circle), History (about one-fifth of the circle), Gym (smaller than History), and Music (the smallest sector, less than one-eighth of the circle). In order of sector size from largest to smallest: Math, Science, History, Gym, Music.

Each of the four response options shows a vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number of Students" ranging from 0 to 35 with grid lines every 5 units, and the horizontal axis showing five subjects: Math, Science, History, Gym, Music.
- Graph A: Math = 30, Science = 25, History = 20, Gym = 17, Music = 8.

- Graph C: Math = 20, Science = 25, History = 30, Gym = 17, Music = 8.

reference_items.figure_description:
The item contains two images:
1. At the top, a circular spinner divided into three sectors: a large dark-grey sector spanning roughly half the circle (bottom-left), a medium grey sector (top-left, spanning roughly one-quarter), and a white sector (right side). An arrow is pivoted at the center pointing toward the upper-right into the white sector.
2. At the bottom, a vertical bar graph titled "Bar graph". The horizontal axis has tick marks labeled "Red", "Blue", and "Green" under three unfilled vertical rectangular bars: the "Red" bar is the tallest (5 grid units high), the "Blue" bar is 3 grid units high, and the "Green" bar is 2 grid units high. The vertical axis on the left has 6 tick marks connected to square answer boxes: the lowest tick mark at the baseline contains a box with the number "0" inside, and above it are 5 empty square boxes aligned with tick marks at heights 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 (matching the tops of the bars at 2, 3, and 5).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
